Personally, if I'm paying a bomb for an item, I expect good hygiene & at least some decent seating both are missing here.
In the early days, there were limited options available but the quality was up to the mark, now there's everything available but no food quality & taste. Putting an insane amount of cheese & cream doesn't make food tasty.
To sum up, try a sandwich, pani puri & dosa without a miss, they're still holding that old times charm.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst Experience!

This was a corporate order, and we ended up waiting over an hour for our food, only to be met with complete disappointment.

Our order was significantly delayed, and despite calling the restaurant multiple times, no one answered. When I contacted the first delivery partner assigned to the order, he informed me that he had returned the parcel to the restaurant because the raita was leaking. What was frustrating was that neither the restaurant nor the delivery partner informed me about this. He then mentioned that another delivery partner would be assigned since he had already waited too long.

When the food finally arrived, we discovered that one of the main items, Kadhai Paneer, was missing. On top of that, none of the raitas or salads that were supposed to accompany the three biryanis were included.

This was a corporate meal, and several people were left hungry due to the missing items and poor handling of the order. As a Swiggy One member who orders regularly, this has been one of the worst experiences I've had. I will never order from Street Foods by Punjab Grill again and would strongly discourage others from doing so.

Very disappointing service and a complete lack of accountability.

Lasooni chaap – 3/5. I’ve had better chaap before; this one wasn’t very soft and leaned slightly on the sweeter side, which didn’t work for me.

featured_reviews.name: pranoy shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
It has amazing food—truly tasty and genuinely delicious. If you’re craving good kulchas, soft naan, or a comforting dal makhani, this place is one of the best options around. Every dish feels thoughtfully prepared and full of flavour.
You absolutely must try the naan sliders. They’re something new, innovative, and honestly fabulous. There are multiple options available, but the spicy one really stands out and is highly recommended. Another highlight is the Amritsari Kulcha—the stuffing is generous, flavourful, and perfectly balanced.
The Paneer Garlic Ginger Dhaniya Kulcha is unique and memorable. The hint of ginger in the kulcha gives it a completely different and refreshing taste. The Naan Dal Makhani combo is a great choice if you want a wholesome meal—the dal makhani is rich, creamy, and cooked to perfection.
Don’t miss the Khichiya Papad Churi—it’s a must-have and very nicely made. The chaas is extremely refreshing, served in super fun bottles, and complements the meal well. For dessert, the rabdi is killer good, and the paneer rolls are different from the usual and definitely worth trying.
The menu is wide with plenty of options for vegetarians. The ambiance is pleasant and works well even for a small party or family gathering. Service is fast, the place is neat and clean, and valet parking is available on weekends. The restaurant is open from 12–4 PM and reopens in the evening for dinner.
Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:

We tried the basic Aloo Pyaaz Kulcha - it is served along with Chole (the exact type which is served with kulchas), the classic Imli-Onion Chutney and pickle. Chole are refillable - as it should be at any place serving kulchas.
The kulchas had a very generous amount of filling and the taste too was just perfect. They’re priced according Mumbai Rates (₹190) but the taste is like home.
Would definitely recommend anyone this place for Kulchas. Only con is it opens at 11:45 AM which is quite late considering we like to have them in breakfast. Will definitely visit again and try other items on the menu.

featured_reviews.name: Prachi vaidya
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're a die-hard fan of North Indian street food, especially Amritsari-style chole kulche, this hidden gem in Ghatkopar is a must-visit! The place serves authentic, buttery kulchas with perfectly spiced chole that pack a punch of flavor in every bite.

The menu offers a variety of stuffed kulchas – from classic aloo and pyaaz to spicy paneer and even cheese-loaded options – all served with tangy chutneys, onion salad, and a generous bowl of flavorful chole. The portion size is more than satisfying, and the pricing is pretty pocket-friendly too.

What makes it even better? Massive seating space! Unlike most street-style joints, this one offers a spacious and clean dining area — perfect for family outings, large groups, or just a chill lunch scene without the chaos.

Highly recommended for anyone craving Delhi-style vibes in Mumbai. A solid 10/10 for food, space, and value!

featured_reviews.name: Rajesh Gohil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing experience at the Radhe Ghatkopar branch.

I had pre-booked 2.5 kg (₹1113) of biryani at 11:00 AM and clearly informed the staff that I needed it by 5:00 PM. When I arrived at 5:00 PM, the staff seemed unaware of the order and started asking who had taken it. After checking with others, they informed me that the biryani is not ready and would take another 30–40 minutes to prepare. If customers have to wait that long despite pre-booking and making full payment in advance, it defeats the purpose of placing an advance order.

The most concerning part was the food quality. Around 1 kg of biryani was left over, so we stored it in the refrigerator overnight. By the next morning, it had spoiled. In comparison, homemade dhokla prepared on the same day and stored under the same conditions remained perfectly fine. This raises concerns about the ingredients, spices, and overall quality standards being maintained.

My observations:
• Excessive waiting time, even for pre-booked orders.
• Food taste and quality is questionable.
• Minimum order quantity is 250 (it's fixed) grams per plate. They never give food in custom quantities as required.
. The cooks are Nepali, and we were expecting a traditional Gujarati taste, unfortunately the taste did not meet our expectations.

Overall, the experience was disappointing and needs significant improvement in both service and quality and taste control.

I give it a negative -5 out of 5 stars.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited The Backbenchers Cafe in Ghatkopar with a friend. It's a small, casual eatery located right outside the station, making it easily accessible for a quick bite.

We ordered Cheese Peri Peri Fries and two Cold Coffees. The fries were crispy and well-seasoned, and the pricing was reasonable. However, the service was quite slow – it took nearly 45 minutes for our order to arrive, which was a letdown given the small size of the café. The cold coffee was average in taste and could definitely be improved.

Overall, it was an okay experience – the food was decent and the location is convenient, but the long wait time and average beverage quality affected the overall impression. Suitable for a casual stop, but service speed needs attention.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place expecting decent food, but the experience left a lot to be desired. The dahi wada, in particular, was quite disappointing. Instead of having a balanced flavor, it leaned heavily toward sweetness, making it feel more like a dessert than a savory dish. On top of that, the wada itself was unusually small and did not seem properly prepared, both in texture and taste.

What stands out most is that the food feels underwhelming for the amount being charged. A restaurant can charge premium prices, but there should be some effort reflected in taste, portion, and preparation. Sadly, that balance felt missing here.

The ambience works if you just want to sit over tea and spend time, but for food that actually satisfies, there are far better options around.

featured_reviews.name: Abbasali Sorangwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
After trying idli sambar, dahi wada, veg pulao, veg cheese sandwich, and Chinese fried rice over multiple visits, I feel this place is better suited for chai and conversations rather than actual dining.

What disappointed me most was the consistency in poor food quality. I gave the idli sambar two chances on two consecutive weeks, hoping the first experience was just a bad day, but unfortunately, it was the same both times. At ₹70, the idli itself felt poorly prepared, and the sambar had a strange sharp taste, almost acidic, as if too much soda had been added. Instead of feeling satisfying, it actually left me with indigestion after both visits.

Pricing would still be acceptable if the quality matched, but that simply was not the case here. Expensive food is understandable, disappointing food at premium prices is not.

Good spot for chai and hanging out, but if you care about food quality and value, I would avoid coming here for dinner.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely Delightful Experience at NEO WELCOME!

We had an amazing time dining at NEO WELCOME. We tried the Mysore Masala Cheese Dosa, and it was simply wow — crispy, flavorful, and cheesy in the best way possible. The Schezwan Fried Rice was tasty and generous in portion, perfect for sharing.

We also tried their Cold Coffee, which was slightly on the sweeter side but still refreshing and enjoyable. The Paneer Paratha and Sada Butter Cheese Dosa were equally satisfying and lived up to the expectations.

What really stood out, apart from the great food, was the excellent service. The staff were very attentive — one of the waiters was constantly going around refilling cold water glasses the moment they were empty. Such thoughtful service is rare and truly appreciated.

Located just outside the station, it’s super convenient to get to. Overall, a fantastic veg restaurant with great food, top-notch service, and a welcoming vibe. Highly recommended and a must-visit!

featured_reviews.name: Eat In Ontario Blog
featured_reviews.review_text:
Time for a little backstory - despite coming to Mumbai every year all through my childhood, l'd never actually eaten in the Khau Galli due to the paranoia around falling ill easily. This time around though, I braved through the paranoia to indulge my inner foodie. And I am so glad I did because it led me to delicious fusion food at Cheese on Fire (Outside, Kesharwala Garden, 101, Khau Galli, Sindhu Wadi, Ghatkopar East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400077). With a fiery grill and expert hands, this stall is renowned for its variety of momo, pizza, and pasta dishes.
We started off the meal with an order of 6 pizza shots to warm up for the meal ahead! A tiny pani puri stuffed with pizza sauce, cheese, and a drop of hot sauce, the dish didn't have too much of the 'pizza' aspect but was delicious nonetheless. With just the right amount of cheese, the tiny puri was filling without being too cloying while the pizza sauce and hot sauce added a tangy and spicy kick to the dish. On the whole, it was a great segue into the Paneer Tandoori Momos.
Watching the Paneer Tandoori Momos being grilled was an experience on its own with the staff quickly flipping the stuffed momos on the tandoor to give its signature smoky flavour. The essence of the momos lay in its crust this time around - the charred flavours of the grill brought out the comforting paneer flavours within, made only better with the variety of chutneys and eggless mayonnaise (highly recommended if you have not tried it already) on the side.
In conquering the Khau Galli apprehensions of my childhood, I stumbled upon the culinary gem, Cheese on Fire, and it was a revelation of flavors and fear-defying indulgence. Should you find yourself in Ghatkopar suddenly craving either momos or pizza, l would highly recommend checking them out!

To hear more about this review, follow us @eatinontario on Instagram, TikTok, & Facebook. ✨🤩🙏

If you’re a fan of authentic, well-made kulchas, Sai Kripa does not disappoint. Their kulchas are:

✅ Perfectly Crisp & Fluffy – The outer layer has a satisfying crispiness, while the inside remains soft and slightly chewy.

✅ Well-Stuffed & Flavorful – Whether it’s aloo, paneer, or mixed stuffing, they don’t skimp on ingredients. The masala is balanced, with a slight tang and spice kick that complements the kulcha beautifully.

✅ Served with the Right Pairings – A good kulcha is incomplete without chole, raita, or chutney, and Sai Kripa gets this right. Their chole is rich and well-spiced, making for a fulfilling combination.

✅ Good Portion & Value for Money – Generous portions at reasonable pricing make it a great choice for a hearty meal.

Overall, if you’re looking for a place that nails a classic North Indian-style kulcha, Sai Kripa is worth a visit.

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
